title: Ziggurat of Aqar Quf (Dur-Kurigalzu)
summary: The ziggurat at Aqar Quf stands in Dur-Kurigalzu, a royal city established in the mid-2nd millennium BC by King Kurigalzu I near Baghdad. Its roughly square base measures close to seventy metres a side, with seven shallow buttresses per side. The Iraqi Directorate of Antiquities held four excavation campaigns there between 1942 and 1946.

uncertainty.note: University of Baghdad gives only 'mid-2nd millennium BC' for the city's establishment; Penn Museum gives no date.
